arml-2011-team-01.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-01.body:
The geometric sequence gives $y=x^2$. The arithmetic sequence gives $y-x=3-y$, so $2y=x+3$, i.e. $2x^2-x-3=0$ and $x=\frac32$ or $x=-1$. Then $y=\frac94$ or $y=1$, so $x+y=\frac{15}4$ or $0$. The maximum is $\frac{15}4$.

**Answer: $\frac{15}{4}$**

arml-2011-team-02.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-02.body:
The smallest positive value of $n-a_k^2$ comes from the largest earlier term $a_k$ with $a_k^2<n$. Every small positive integer appears early in the sequence, so for $m^2<n\le(m+1)^2$ the best choice is $a_k=m$ and $a_n=n-m^2$. Thus for $m^2+1\le n\le(m+1)^2$ the terms run through $1,2,\dots,2m+1$ (for example $a_2,a_3,a_4=1,2,3$ and $a_5,\dots,a_9=1,\dots,5$), with sum $S_m=\frac{(2m+1)(2m+2)}2=2m^2+3m+1$.

The terms $a_2,\dots,a_{49}$ are the blocks $m=1,\dots,6$, with sums $6,15,28,45,66,91$ (total $251$); also $a_1=1$ and $a_{50}=50-7^2=1$. So the sum is $1+251+1=253$.

**Answer: 253**

arml-2011-team-03.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-03.body:
$253_b\cdot341_b=(2b^2+5b+3)(3b^2+4b+1)=6b^4+23b^3+31b^2+17b+3$. The leading digit $7$ forces a carry out of the $b^3$ place, so $6b^4+23b^3+\cdots\ge7b^4$, which gives $b\le24$. The units digit is $Z=3$. Then $6b^4+23b^3+31b^2+17b=7b^4+4b^3+Xb^2+Yb$, and dividing by $b$:
$$b^3+Xb+Y=19b^2+31b+17.$$
Reducing modulo $b$ gives $Y\equiv17\pmod b$. For $b\ge18$ this means $Y=17$, and then $b^2+X=19b+31$, i.e. $b(b-19)=31-X\le31$ with $b>19$: only $b=20$, $X=11$. (The bases $6\le b\le17$ fail by direct check: the leading digit or the second digit does not match.)

Check: $253_{20}=903$, $341_{20}=1281$, $903\cdot1281=1{,}156{,}743=7\cdot20^4+4\cdot20^3+11\cdot20^2+17\cdot20+3$. ✓

**Answer: 20**

arml-2011-team-04.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-04.body:
The curve is at most $10\pi$, and $4x>10\pi$ for $x>\frac{5\pi}2$, so all intersections lie in $0\le x\le\frac{5\pi}2$. Since $10\pi\sin^2x=5\pi-5\pi\cos2x$, the curve is symmetric about the point $A=\left(\frac{5\pi}4,5\pi\right)$, and the line $y=4x$ passes through $A$, so the picture is symmetric under the half-turn about $A$. Label the intersection points of the line and the curve $O,D,B,A,C,E,F$ in order of increasing $x$ (with $O$ the origin). The half-turn swaps $O\leftrightarrow F$, $D\leftrightarrow E$, $B\leftrightarrow C$. The line lies below the curve exactly on the segments $DB$, $AC$, $EF$ (and above it on $OD$, $BA$, $CE$).

By the symmetry, $AC=AB$ and $EF=OD$, so the total length below the curve is
$$DB+AC+EF=DB+AB+OD=OA=\sqrt{\left(\tfrac{5\pi}4\right)^2+(5\pi)^2}=\frac{5\pi}4\sqrt{1+16}=\frac{5\pi\sqrt{17}}4.$$

**Answer: $\frac{5\pi\sqrt{17}}{4}$**

arml-2011-team-05.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-05.body:
Let $m\angle B=\alpha$. Then $m\angle F=\alpha$, $m\angle D=2\alpha$, $m\angle C=m\angle E=5\alpha$, $m\angle A=10\alpha$, and the angle sum $24\alpha=720^\circ$ gives $\alpha=30^\circ$: $\angle B=\angle F=30^\circ$, $\angle D=60^\circ$, $\angle C=\angle E=150^\circ$, and $\angle A=300^\circ$ (reflex).

Let $s$ be the common side length. $\triangle CDE$ has $CD=DE=s$ and $\angle D=60^\circ$, so it is equilateral with $CE=s$. Then $\angle BCE=150^\circ-60^\circ=90^\circ$ and likewise $\angle CEF=90^\circ$, and $BC=EF=CE=s$, so $BCEF$ is a square of side $s$ with diagonal $BE=3$; its area is $\frac{3^2}2=\frac92$. At $A$ the reflex angle means the triangle $BAF$ (with $AB=AF=s$ and $\angle BAF=360^\circ-300^\circ=60^\circ$) is a congruent equilateral triangle lying inside the square. Thus the hexagon is the square with the triangle $BAF$ removed and the congruent triangle $CDE$ added:
$$[ABCDEF]=[BCEF]-[BAF]+[CDE]=[BCEF]=\frac92.$$

**Answer: $\frac92$**

arml-2011-team-06.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-06.body:
Let $A=(0,5)$, $B=(12,0)$, $C=(1,-1)$. Then $d(A,C)+d(B,C)=(1+6)+(11+1)=19$, so $s=19$.

For $P=(x,y)$ with $0\le x\le12$ and $y=-1$: $d(A,P)+d(B,P)=x+6+(12-x)+1=19$, so the whole segment from $(0,-1)$ to $(12,-1)$ is on the curve; likewise the segment from $(0,6)$ to $(12,6)$ ($0\le x\le12$, $y=6$), and the vertical segments $x=-1$ and $x=13$ for $0\le y\le5$. At the corners the curve consists of diagonal segments, e.g. for $P=(x,y)$ with $x\ge12$, $y\le0$: $d(A,P)+d(B,P)=2x-2y-7=19$, i.e. $x-y=13$, the segment from $(12,-1)$ to $(13,0)$; similarly the segments from $(13,5)$ to $(12,6)$, $(0,6)$ to $(-1,5)$ and $(-1,0)$ to $(0,-1)$.

So the "ellipse" is the octagon obtained from the rectangle $[-1,13]\times[-1,6]$ (area $14\cdot7=98$) by cutting off four corner triangles, each with legs $1$ and $1$ (area $\frac12$). The area is $98-4\cdot\frac12=96$.

**Answer: 96**

arml-2011-team-07.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-07.body:
Substituting $f(1)=\frac{f(2)}{512}$ into $\frac1{f(1)}=2f(2)$ gives $\frac{512}{f(2)}=2f(2)$, so $f(2)^2=256$ and $f(2)=16$ (positive). Then $f(1)=\frac1{32}$.

By the recursion: $f(3)=f(2)f(1)=\frac12$, $f(4)=f(3)f(2)=8$. So we need $f(8)$: $f(5)=f(4)f(3)=4$, $f(6)=f(5)f(4)=32$, $f(7)=f(6)f(5)=128$, $f(8)=f(7)f(6)=4096$.

(Alternatively, with $g(n)=\log_2f(n)$: $g(1)=-5$, $g(2)=4$, and $g$ obeys the Fibonacci recursion, so $g(8)=12$ and $f(8)=2^{12}$.)

**Answer: 4096**

arml-2011-team-08.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-08.body:
Reversing the coefficients replaces each zero $r$ by $\frac1r$, so whenever $r$ is a zero of the polynomial so is $\frac1r$. Since all zeros are integers, each zero is $\pm1$. With $\gcd$ of the coefficients equal to $1$, the leading coefficient must be $\pm1$, so
$$f(x)=\pm(x+1)^k(x-1)^{n-k},\qquad0\le k\le n.$$
Each of these has reversed polynomial with the same zeros (the zeros $\pm1$ are self-reciprocal), and they are all distinct. So there are $2(n+1)$ polynomials of degree $n$, and the total for $1\le n\le7$ is $2(2+3+\cdots+8)=2\cdot35=70$.

**Answer: 70**

arml-2011-team-09.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-09.body:
Label the sides $s_0,s_1,\dots,s_{15}$. Two sides meet at a vertex of the polygon iff they are adjacent, so the three chosen sides must be pairwise nonadjacent. The shape of the triangle (its angles) depends only on the *spacings* between the chosen sides, so the problem reduces to integers $a,b,c\ge2$ with $a+b+c=16$ (the numbers of steps between consecutive chosen sides). Diametrically opposite sides are parallel and cannot both be used, so none of $a,b,c$ equals $8$. Reflections and rotations give congruent triangles, so we count unordered triples $a\ge b\ge c$:

$(12,2,2),(11,3,2),(10,4,2),(10,3,3),(9,5,2),(9,4,3),(7,7,2),(7,6,3),(7,5,4),(6,6,4),(6,5,5)$.

(The excluded triples containing an $8$ are $(8,6,2),(8,5,3),(8,4,4)$.) That is $11$ triangles.

**Answer: 11**

arml-2011-team-10.title: Solution
arml-2011-team-10.body:
The overlap is an octagon; the part of the rotated square outside the overlap consists of four congruent right triangles, one at each corner, each with legs $x,y$ and hypotenuse $z$, where $x=z\sin\theta$ and $y=z\cos\theta$ (the acute angle of the triangle is $\theta$). Their total area is $9-8=1$, so $4\cdot\frac{xy}2=1$ and $2xy=1$.

Each side of the rotated square (length $3$) is cut by the lower square into a leg $y$ of one corner triangle, then a segment $z$ (the hypotenuse of a corner triangle of the other square), then a leg $x$ of the next corner triangle: $x+y+z=3$. With $x^2+y^2=z^2$:
$$(x+y)^2=(3-z)^2\ \Rightarrow\ z^2+2xy=9-6z+z^2\ \Rightarrow\ 1=9-6z\ \Rightarrow\ z=\tfrac43.$$
Hence $\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\dfrac{x+y}z=\dfrac{3-z}z=\dfrac{5/3}{4/3}=\dfrac54$.

**Answer: $\frac54$**
